Three failure modes you'll use to read

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.
Every backward reference points at a beat that exists.
Live-demo beats survive a text read.

rules_evaluated.evidence: chunk 1 "What would have caught this earlier?": line 7: "Not *did the task succeed*. Not *should I have spec'd it tighter*. A diagnostic: you read the artefact, you find what went wrong, and for each thing you ask this one question." — harm rule 7's first sub-item guards against: the templated 'Not X. Not Y. Z.' rhetorical tic reading as formulaic filler rather than direct statement. This line is a verbatim instance of that exact shape (two negated candidate-questions then a declarative landing on 'A diagnostic'); no maintainer accept-note covers this passage, so the harm is live, not merely theoretical. All other rule-7 sub-items (anaphora triples, self-grading superlatives, number+retraction, abstraction stacks, empty-leg verb triplets) checked clean across all chunks — 'statistical machine with a finite window' (chunk 3) is grounded by its own next clause and maintainer-attested as deliberate, not an abstraction stack.
rules_evaluated.fix_hint: Recast as one declarative, e.g. 'The question that drives the read is diagnostic, not evaluative: what would have caught this earlier in the session?' — drop the two 'Not ___' negations.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
Presence precedes content — verify against the composed deck, not long-read.
Numbering — position is computed, content ordinals are linted.
